column7: LOCKED IN. Steam range settled at 0.5MPa (5 bar) deliberately matched to a planned mechanical OPV at ~5 bar on the steam line: the OPV is the real system pressure ceiling in both normal and fault operation, so the sensor gets best resolution across the whole range the system will ever actually see, and clipping past full scale costs nothing because the OPV is already acting there. Sensor survival was never the issue (150% FS overload = 7.5 bar, above the JYPC-4 pump 5.5 bar deadhead); the question was measurement validity, and the OPV resolves it. Instantaneous 50-100Hz vibration-pump ripple is not resolvable by this sensor regardless of range (~0.1s settle time acts as an anti-alias filter), so finer resolution on the averaged signal it does report is the sound trade. OPV setpoint and sensor full scale must be chosen together, not independently. Also reports temperature over I2C per-unit (16-bit Q8.8) - expected to be laggy (internal compensation element, not a fast direct-contact probe, thermal mass/path between water and sensing element). Candidate use: the brew-line unit's temp reading, if placed near the group head/exit-to-coffee, could serve as a secondary/diagnostic signal for actual delivered temperature or group readiness - NOT the fast primary control loop, which stays on the thermoblock's own NTC. Response time not yet bench-characterized. Not yet authored to the graph - worth carrying forward if used for real
